name: Axel

hlido_opinion.headline: A native-Mac control room for dispatching coding agents — a thoughtful niche tool with a strong approval model, judged on a thin public surface.
hlido_opinion.body: Axel is a macOS app that treats AI coding agents as a task queue: add tasks, pick which agent (Claude, Codex, OpenCode, Antigravity) runs each, reorder priorities live, and watch them execute in parallel. The details it chose to build are the encouraging part — a single approval inbox where every file edit, command, and API call needs explicit permission (with diff preview and auto-approve rules), portable skill files symlinked into each agent's expected location, and git-worktree + tmux session spawning per branch. For a developer running several coding agents at once, that human-in-the-loop control surface is exactly the missing piece, and 'nothing runs without approval' is a genuinely good default. The heavy caveat, and the reason this review carries low confidence: the public surface is thin — a single captured screenshot, no pricing shown, macOS-only, and a young vendor (© 2025 Txtx, Inc.) — so this is a promising-looking, narrowly-scoped utility assessed from its landing page, not a verified evaluation. Treat the score as provisional pending a fuller, hands-on review.

tier_rationale: STEADY (70) at low confidence: the design choices visible on the surface are strong (explicit per-action approval inbox, portable skills, worktree/tmux orchestration for dispatching coding agents). Kept at the band floor and flagged low-confidence because the public evidence is thin (one screenshot, no pricing), the product is macOS-only, and the vendor is early — the score is provisional pending a hands-on review.
what_it_does_well: Explicit approval inbox — every file edit, command, and API call is gated with diff/preview and auto-approve rules
Multi-agent dispatch from one queue (Claude, Codex, OpenCode, Antigravity), reorderable while running
Portable skills: one skill file symlinked into each agent’s expected location at launch
Per-branch git worktree + tmux session spawning; sessions persist and reattach
Native macOS app with keyboard-first control and token/cost tracking
what_it_fails_at: Very thin public surface (single captured screenshot) — limits confidence in this assessment
No pricing disclosed on the reviewed surface
Early vendor with no public track record or reliability evidence
best_for: Mac developers running multiple coding agents who want tight human-in-the-loop approval
Users who value keyboard-driven, local orchestration over cloud dashboards
Teams standardizing on portable skill files across agents
not_recommended_for: Buyers who need transparent pricing before trialing
Anyone needing a proven, mature orchestration platform today
